title: Slice governance playbook for hybrid A/B experiments
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a compact governance model and practical checklist for cross-functional activation of hybrid experiments (canary + A/B) across Redwood's operations surface. Focus: minimize blast radius, keep latency/cost budgets predictable, and make human handoffs explicit.

Scope:
- Applies to feature rollouts that change inference routing, model variant selection, or introduce new prompt-level transformations.
- Intended for product owners, experiment owners, SRE, Observability, Solutions/SE, and CS when customer-visible behavior can change.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Define slices early (owner, rationale, size, instrumentation).
- Have a two-layer gate: telemetry signal gate + human approval gate.
- Use a traffic-thinning strategy: synthetic smoke -> small live cohorts -> staggered ramp -> plateau -> full exposure.
- Predeclare fallbacks and cost/latency reversion thresholds.

Key roles and responsibilities (one-liners):
- Experiment Owner: owns hypothesis, primary contact, must present runbook.
- Traffic Steward: configures slice weights in the orchestrator and watches throttles.
- Observability Lead: defines metrics, retention keys, and dashboard links.
- SRE Oncall: ensures infra limits, enforces circuit-breakers.
- Safety Reviewer: flags behavior/regression risk and approves human-check window.
- Customer Success point: pre-notified for externally visible changes.

Slice definition template (fill before activation):
- slice-name: short tag e.g. search-clarity-v2-small-cohort
- owner: name + slack handle
- purpose/hypothesis: 1-2 sentences
- inclusion criteria: user filters (platform, locale, premium tier, quota)
- sample size and ramp plan: baseline % -> target % -> estimated traffic qps
- metrics: primary metric(s) + guardrail metrics (latency p95, error rate, token cost)
- data retention & IDs: which request fields to persist for postmortem
- fallback plan: model variant or routing fallback details
- duration and cadence: how long to run at each stage and decision cadence

Telemetry gates (must be in place before any live traffic):
1) Baseline dashboards created and linkable from runbook (Observability Lead).
2) Synthetic/regression test sweep: pass smoke tests (latency < threshold, no crash).
3) Canary statistical gate: run an A/B calculator with min sample requirements.
4) Cost guardrail: projected per-token cost delta does not exceed budget x%.
5) Safety checks: content-safety quick-run (if applicable) and manual review.

Staged rollout pattern (recommended):
- Stage 0: Dry-run on synthetic traffic in staging. Objective: surface obvious failures and resource regressions.
- Stage 1: Micro-canary 0.05% to 0.5% sample with human-in-loop watch (30–60m).
- Stage 2: Small cohorts 1–5% with automated telemetry gate at 1h and 6h.
- Stage 3: Broad test 10–25% with daily checks and cost sampling.
- Stage 4: Ramp to target (if target >25%) only after cross-team signoff and no signal breaches for N cycles.

Traffic thinning / rehydration recipe (notes to self):
- If signal breach occurs, thin traffic by halving the slice weight every X minutes until stable.
- Rehydration (bring traffic back): reverse sequence but add a forced observation window after each doubling.
- Use synthetic replays to test rehydration before flipping weights back.

Operational checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] Slice definition completed and shared (link runbook in doc header).
- [ ] Dashboards deployed and baseline anchors tagged.
- [ ] Owners and oncall paged and calendar blocked for the first 6 hours.
- [ ] Customer Success notified (if >5% visible changes).
- [ ] Risk register created in Confluence (CONFLUENCE-9876).
- [ ] Rollback playbook drafted with explicit traffic + model commands.
- [ ] Experiment token/cost estimate uploaded.

Run cadence and decision rules (suggested):
- Decision windows: 30m micro-checks during first 2 hours, 6h checks until 24h, daily for next 7 days.
- If primary metric regression p < 0.05 in opposite direction and effect size > minimum detectable effect, pause and investigate.
- If latency p95 increases by > 25% or errors double baseline, immediate throttle to 10% and SRE pager.
- If cost/unit increases by > 40% and no quality improvement, revert.

Comms templates (short):
- Slack to #release-ops: "Launching slice search-clarity-v2-small-cohort 2025-03-02 09:00PT. Micro-canary 0.1% for 60m. Owners: Maya Patel (@maya). Dashboards: <link>. Pager: @sre-oncall. If you observe visible regressions, post to #incidents and tag owners"
- Email to CS: "Heads-up: A/B test 'search-clarity' begins 2025-03-02. Visible to ~1% of customers initially. Contact: Priya Singh."

Post-launch artifact checklist:
- [ ] Decision log record (why kept, why rolled back).
- [ ] Sampled request/response artifacts stored with IDs for 30d.
- [ ] Cost/latency delta report for first 72h.
- [ ] Regression eval on critical prompt set.
- [ ] Postmortem for any incident, follow the incident template.

Open questions and follow-ups (action items):
- Who owns the canonical registry of slice-names? Proposal: Traffic Steward team. ACTION: Evan to propose registry format by 2025-02-18.
- How to automate the cost-guardrail check in orchestration? Investigate adding a preflight cost-simulation step to PRs. ACTION: Carlos to prototype.
- Should we require a human safety review for changes that touch prompt transforms even if the model doesn't change? Proposal: yes for any transform that rewrites user text. ACTION: Priya to draft a short safety checklist.

Mini-examples (to copy into runbooks):
- Example slice: support-clarity-v1-cohortA
  owner: Evan Liu (@evan)
  hypothesis: reduce followup question rate by surfacing clarifying info
  inclusion: web users, EN-US, tier=free
  ramp: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% (48h at each step)
  metrics: followup-rate (primary), latency p95 (guardrail), token-cost per session (guardrail)

- Example quick rollback command (operator):
  1) set-slice-weight support-clarity-v1 0.0 --via=orchestrator
  2) route-default-model stable-v1
  3) trigger-alerts "slice-rollback" and notify #release-ops

Notes to self / heuristics we've learned:
- Keep slices as semantically simple as possible. Too many orthogonal filters explode cardinality for telemetry and increase false positives in stats.
- Prefer human-in-loop for first 24 hours on any LLM-behavior change. ML drift is subtle.
- A/B windows should be long enough to catch low-frequency failure modes (recommend 72h sample for behavior tests).

References and anchors:
- Runbooks glossary: confluence.redwood/runbooks/llm-slices (CONFLUENCE-9876)
- Orchestrator PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-orchestrator/pull/89
- Example JIRA for past canary incident: JIRA-RDW-1234

Appendix: quick decision tree (text form)
- Smoke tests fail? -> Stop, fix, retest in staging.
- Micro-canary shows latency spike? -> Throttle to 10% and escalate SRE.
- Primary metric neutral, guardrails OK, cost small delta? -> Continue ramp.
- Primary metric improves but cost large? -> Discuss product tradeoff; consider hybrid routing based on traffic classes.

Last notes: keep this doc lean and copy sections into per-experiment runbooks. The goal is low-friction reproducible patterns so teams don't reinvent throttle/fallback steps every time.

-- Maya
